Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Adult patient with 5–6 days of dry, persistent cough (day and night), rhinorrhea, chills/shivering, myalgias, fatigue; no chest pain; no day-to-day dyspnea (only during coughing fits); initial mild diarrhea resolved. Past history significant for type 2 diabetes and hypertension (on metformin and lisinopril).
- Most consistent with an acute viral respiratory illness (viral URI/acute viral bronchitis). COVID-19 and influenza remain plausible given symptom cluster and lack of testing. Community-acquired pneumonia considered less likely at present due to absence of dyspnea, chest pain, sputum, or documented abnormal vitals. ACE inhibitor–induced cough considered less likely given acute onset with viral prodrome.
- Plan per clinician: Conservative management—rest, maintain hydration, use acetaminophen for symptom relief (dose/route/frequency not documented), consider taking 1–2 days off work to reduce transmission and facilitate recovery. Safety net: return if not improving in 2–3 days or sooner if breathing worsens. If still feverish and cough not improving, antibiotics for possible chest infection may be considered.
- Lifestyle counseling: Reduce alcohol intake (graduated reduction advised).

Management Plan
- Rest, fluids, and acetaminophen for symptom control (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Short-term work exclusion (1–2 days) advised.
- Return/seek care sooner if breathing worsens; re-evaluate in 2–3 days if no improvement; antibiotics may be considered if persistent feverishness and ongoing cough.
- Alcohol reduction counseling provided.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute viral respiratory infection (common cold/acute viral bronchitis) — High likelihood: Short duration dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias; no dyspnea or chest pain.
- COVID-19 — Moderate likelihood: Dry cough, chills, myalgias, fatigue, and transient diarrhea fit; no testing performed.
- Influenza — Moderate likelihood: Systemic symptoms with myalgias/chills and cough within a typical time course.
